scenario: File-mode login issues a token whose scopes match the user's roles
preconditions: platform-api with auth.mode=file and seeded admin, publisher, developer users
steps: 1) POST /api/portal/v0.9/auth/login for each seeded user 2) decode token
expected_result: 200; RS256 JWT; scope claim equals the role-to-scope expansion for the user's roles
existing_coverage: Partial: ui login.feature (through AI Workspace UI only)

scenario: Login with wrong password or unknown user is rejected
steps: POST login with bad password; POST login with unknown user
expected_result: 401 for both; no token; same error body for both (no user enumeration)

scenario: Every /api/v0.9 resource family rejects a request without a token
steps: Scenario outline over GET/POST on projects, rest-apis, gateways, secrets, applications, subscriptions, api-portals, llm-providers, mcp-proxies, agent-proxies, graphql-apis
expected_result: 401 for every row; no resource data in the body

scenario: A role without the required scope gets 403; reads allowed for viewer
preconditions: Users with ap_viewer, ap_publisher, ap_subscriber, ap_operator, ap_admin roles
steps: Scenario outline: each role performs create / read / delete on REST API, gateway, secret, subscription plan
expected_result: Allowed operations succeed; others 403 with a scope message; no partial state change on 403

scenario: ap:api_key:all:manage lets an admin manage another user's API key
steps: Publisher B deletes the key; admin with ap:api_key:all:manage deletes the key

scenario: Scope mode and role mode grant the same effective access
preconditions: Two platform-api configs: authorization.mode=scope and mode=role
notes: Needs a platform-api overlay per mode

scenario: authorization.enabled=false lets any authenticated caller through
steps: Token with no ap: scopes calls POST /rest-apis

steps: Call API with valid token; wrong issuer; wrong audience; expired; tampered signature

scenario: Nested claim mapping (e.g. realm_access.roles) resolves roles
steps: Token with nested roles calls a publisher-only route

expected_result: 401 for the first three; 200 for the valid gateway token
